summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 57% YoY to ₹149.23 crore and EBITDA margin hit 14.35%, but margins were marginally lower QoQ on cost pressures.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was ₹149.23 crore, up 57% YoY and 17% QoQ, driven by higher volumes and better capacity utilisation. EBITDA rose to ₹21.41 crore (14.35% margin, up 769 bps YoY) and PAT to ₹13.49 crore from ₹0.54 crore. Management said margins were slightly lower sequentially because fixed-price contracts blocked immediate pass-through of higher freight and raw material costs, and because of forex and investment mark-to-market provisions. FY26 revenue was ₹500.95 crore (+36%), EBITDA ₹72.69 crore (14.51% margin) and PAT ₹48.13 crore (+128%). Phase II commissioning slipped to early Q2 FY27 due to gas and labour shortages, with commercial production still guided for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Animal API
segments.commentary: Core business, contributing 95% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Top 10 customers were 29% of sales and top 10 products 66%. Company now offers about 45 APIs versus about 20 three years ago.

segments.name: Regulated markets (Europe/US)
segments.commentary: Europe sales expected to start in FY27 and US in FY28, with significant revenue from FY28. Europe has three CEPs approved, three under review and two being prepared; US VMS filings are five done with six planned this year.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin target of 15% to 18%; management said the company is close to this band, with Q1 FY27 possibly 1-2% lower as price increases only started flowing mid-quarter and margins expected from Q2 onwards.
Partial price pass-through achieved in Q1 FY27; management declined to quantify the overall price increase.
Phase II (Tarapur greenfield) commissioning moved to early Q2 FY27 from Q1 FY27; commercial production still targeted for H2 FY27.
Expected total Phase II capex of ₹210 crore, of which ₹182.75 crore was spent up to Q4 FY26; ongoing capex after completion estimated at ₹15-20 crore.
New expansion revenue potential of up to ₹350 crore turnover, to be reached over three to four years; the company declined to combine it with existing-plant revenue.
Regulated market margins expected to be 3-5 percentage points higher than the 15-18% band, but management declined to give regulated revenue figures.
capex_capacity: Phase I of the expansion is contributing meaningfully and is operating at about 70-80% utilisation, with Q4 volumes absorbed within it.
Phase II includes five clean rooms and is expected to be commissioned in early Q2 FY27, with commercial production from H2 FY27.

Phase II capex rose from ₹160 crore to ₹210 crore: about ₹20 crore for automation and digitisation and about ₹50 crore from higher metal costs; management said the increase will not add sales capacity.
Brownfield expansion of existing facilities is planned for FY27 to add ROW capacity.
Peak utilisation of the new plant is expected to take three to four years.
Company outsources about 20% of its intermediate requirements.
demand_pricing: Volume growth reported across geographies, with Latin America a successful new market and customer count up 47 QoQ on new country registrations.
Competition from Chinese and Indian players continues; price erosion on fluralaner has largely settled, and Chinese producers have begun raising prices from April/May 2026.
Oversupply in 2024 and 2025 drove price erosion; management does not expect return to prior 20-21% margins for at least two to three years.
Management plans to add 9-10 new products per year, and five new APIs were added in Q4.
Fixed-price contracts delayed pass-through of freight and raw material cost increases linked to geopolitical developments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue run rate from Phase I without Phase II, and how is outsourcing contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a run rate of about ₹150 crore per quarter from Phase I plus outsourcing, with 10-15% growth on top; Phase II's five clean rooms commission next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the USFDA inspection and the Phase II utilisation until then?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the audit timing depends on the regulator and could fall in 2026 or 2027; until then Phase II will serve ROW and Europe, with European business expected in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How many CEPs and DMFs are approved, and when will the rest come through?
qa_highlights.answer: Three CEPs are registered and three are under review, with a ~18-month review period; management expects six CEPs and nine DMFs by year-end 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise ₹10-11 crore QoQ, and how much was forex loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to mark-to-market provisioning on forex and investments; it did not have the exact forex figure on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to hit a higher margin band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is 15-18% EBITDA margin and it is close; it said partial pass-through is done and China has started raising prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation and dividend plan given the debt and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth capex is funded internally without new borrowing, and it has not yet set a dividend strategy for three years out.

risks_watch: USFDA audit timing is entirely at the regulator's discretion, and US regulated revenue could slip beyond FY28.
Phase II commissioning already slipped one quarter due to gas and labour shortages.
Fixed-price contracts and the lag in pass-through leave margins exposed to crude-linked freight and raw material inflation; Q1 FY27 margins may be 1-2% lower.
Forex and investment mark-to-market provisions weighed on Q4 margins and other expenses; the amount was not disclosed.
Chinese supply and capacity could keep pressure on prices and limit recovery to the earlier 20%+ margin range.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and the 15-18% margin target, but cautious and evasive on specifics: they declined to quantify price increases, regulated revenue, forex losses, dividend policy and USFDA timing.

We do not look at just the geography. So, we will move certain products into that particular plant.
Some companies do not want to change their supply chain so easily. They look for a substantial saving before they change.
